name: AS-ViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.6 at 3.0 GFLOPs (f=0.65; baseline 79.8 at 4.6)
notes: Class attention weighted by a per-token head importance (l2-norm of each head's context) scores tokens; three learnable thresholds before stages 2-4 keep tokens whose score exceeds the threshold, so the count varies per image. Thresholds are trained with a budget-aware FLOPs loss and distillation during 30-epoch fine-tuning. Throughput on one 2080Ti at batch 64; latency is single-image (6.56 ms vs 6.16 ms for DeiT-S). Code URL is from the arXiv comment, not the paper body. Not an RL method.
evidence: "learnable parameters are inserted as thresholds to distinguish informative tokens from unimportant ones" (Abstract); "We keep tokens with scores greater than the threshold" (3.3); "We finetune the pre-trained model by 30 epoch to obtain the compressed network" (4.1)

name: METR
backbones: DeiT-S; DeiT-B; MAE ViT-B; MAE ViT-L
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.64 at 3.0 GFLOPs (METR+EViT, 30-epoch fine-tuning; EViT 79.32; baseline 79.82 at 4.6)
notes: Adds early-exit heads with self-distillation in every reduction block during training so that early [CLS] attention becomes a reliable token score; heads are removed after training. Built on EViT (keep ratio at blocks 4, 7, 10, inattentive tokens fused into one) or on DiffRate (prune+merge with learned rates). Also reports from-scratch (79.76) and 100-epoch (80.09) settings for DeiT-S at 3.0 GFLOPs. Throughput 3582 img/s is from Table 1 (keep ratio 0.7, 3.0 GFLOPs, RTX 4090, batch 512), the same reduction setting. No code URL in the paper.
evidence: "By injecting early task pressure via multi-exit loss, the [CLS] token is spurred to collect task-related information in even early blocks, thus bolstering the credibility of [CLS] attention as a token-scoring metric" (Abstract); "reduce the number of tokens according to the specified keep ratio (e.g. 30% of the tokens are reduced when keep ratio set to 0.7) in the 4-th, 7-th, and 10-th blocks, and fuse the unimportant tokens into one additional token" (Sec. 4); "for those without special notation we start from supervised checkpoints and fine-tune for 30 epochs" (Table 5)

name: STAR
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.4 at 2.6 GFLOPs (STAR, rho=0.75; baseline 79.8 at 4.6)
notes: Online [CLS] attention (intra-layer) is fused with offline LRP relevance (inter-layer, computed on training data) as a weighted product; top-k tokens are kept per layer. Per-layer keep rates are set offline from the average cosine similarity of tokens with one knob rho (same for every image). The a-STAR variant uses the rates as CDF percentiles, so the count varies per image (DeiT-S 79.3 at 2.5, 3843.7 img/s). Fine-tuned 120 epochs with hard distillation. Throughput on A100, batch 128, FP32. Code URL from the PDF hyperlink. Not RL.
evidence: "patches are successively pruned at each layer by maintaining only the top-k most important ones" (Abstract); "we propose an automated method for selecting them based on offline-derived metrics" (Abstract); "The pruned models are fine-tuned for 120 epochs with hard distillation" (Sec. 6)

name: LF-ViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.8 at 1.7 GFLOPs (m=5, eta=0.47; baseline 79.8 at 4.6)
notes: Localization stage on a 112x112 downsampled image (7x7 tokens); if the confidence is below eta, NGCA (sliding-window sum of EMA class attention) picks an m x m region, and the top alpha*m^2 tokens of that region from the full-resolution image go to the focus stage, while other tokens are reused from the localization stage. Trained 350 epochs with the DeiT recipe; no pre-trained checkpoint is mentioned, so training is taken as from scratch. Throughput on one A100, batch 1024. Not RL.
evidence: "In the Localization phase, a reduced-resolution image is processed; if a definitive prediction remains elusive, our pioneering Neighborhood Global Class Attention (NGCA) mechanism is triggered" (Abstract); "we select the highest GCA α × m2 tokens from the localized class-discriminative regions in the original image as the input of the focus stage" (Focus Inference Stage); "We train LF-ViT for a total of 350 epochs" (Implementation Details)

name: LTRP
backbones: MAE ViT-B; MAE ViT-L; MAE ViT-H (ranking model ViT-S or ViT-T)
main_result: ViT-B: top-1 83.1 at 13.1 GFLOPs (keep ratio 0.75, ViT-T ranking model; baseline 83.3 at 17.6)
notes: Input-level patch selection before the backbone. A separate ranking model learns with ListMLE to rank patches by self-supervised pseudo scores (change of the MAE reconstruction when a visible patch is removed); top-k patches plus a few DPC-KNN cluster representatives from homogeneous regions are kept at a fixed keep ratio. The classifier is initialized from the MAE encoder and trained on the kept patches. GPU/CPU throughput reported (3090 server; batch size not stated). No DeiT-S ImageNet-1k result (ViT-S only on ImageNet-100). Not RL.
evidence: "inferring the semantic density score of each patch by quantifying variation between reconstructions with and without this patch, and learning to rank the patches with the pseudo score" (Abstract); "Top-k patches are selected using the trained ranking model and fed into downstream tasks" (Fig. 2); "They are both initialized from the MAE encoder" (Sec. 4.1)

name: VTC-LFC
notes: Joint channel and token pruning. Token score combines low-frequency energy (LFE) with head-weighted CLS attention; channels are scored by low-frequency sensitivity (Taylor). Bottom-up cascade pruning sets per-block token and channel counts offline on 5000 training images under an allowed accuracy drop (same for every image); then 150-epoch fine-tuning (DeiT-S) with hard distillation. Table 1 gives only the FLOPs reduction ratio, Table 6 gives 2.1 GFLOPs for the same 79.4% model. Throughput on one V100, batch 256. Not RL.
evidence: "Two metrics named low-frequency sensitivity (LFS) and low-frequency energy (LFE) are proposed for better channel pruning and token pruning" (Abstract); "During compression of each block, the number of tokens is gradually reduced until the performance drop reaches" (Bottom-up Cascade Pruning); "After pruning, the compressed models are fine-tuned with hard distillation" (Sec. 4)

name: DyT
main_result: ViT-B/16: VTAB-1K mean top-1 77.14 at 12.54 GFLOPs (r=0.5; full tuning 68.96 at 17.58)
notes: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning method. A linear token dispatcher per block (threshold 0.5, Gumbel noise in training) decides which tokens enter the MLP; deactivated tokens skip the block and are processed only by a parallel adapter, so the token count is not reduced (operation other, closest to a per-block halt). Only adapters and dispatchers are trained (0.16 M parameters). 912.30 img/s on V100 at batch 512. Main purpose is efficient adaptation; token skipping is the inference-efficiency mechanism. Not RL.
evidence: "we propose a token dispatcher to distinguish informative tokens from less important ones, allowing the latter to dynamically skip the original block" (Abstract); "Then, we set 0.5 as the threshold to determine the activation of each token" (Sec. 3.2); "DyT does not reduce the total number of tokens, making it suitable for both visual recognition and dense prediction scenarios" (Introduction)

name: MG-ViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.8 at 2.0 GFLOPs (eps=0.49; baseline 79.8 at 4.6)
notes: Two stages: 7x7 tokens first; if the top softmax score is below eps, head and middle patches (by EMA global class attention) are re-split 3x3 and 2x2 with feature reuse. The slimming module keeps positive tokens, merges boundary tokens by bipartite cosine matching on value vectors, and fuses negative tokens into one. Hierarchical variant on PVT-S for COCO and ADE20K. Trained 300 epochs following the DeiT and LV-ViT recipes; no checkpoint is mentioned, so training is taken as from scratch. Throughput on RTX 3090 (batch not stated). No code URL. Not RL.
evidence: "In single-granularity inference stage, an input image is split into a small number of patches for simple inference" (Abstract); "Boundary and negative tokens are respectively merged by different rules to reduce their numbers" (Introduction); "use AdamW optimizer to train all models for 300 epochs" (Appendix 7.2)

name: ToFe
notes: An MLP + Gumbel-softmax selector before blocks 4, 7, 10 splits tokens into kept and frozen; frozen tokens skip blocks, get a bottleneck-MLP approximation, and can be reused at later stages (halt with later reuse). Budget-aware FLOPs loss; the instance-adaptive mode uses the per-image mask, the batch-adaptive mode keeps the top-N average count. 30-epoch training from pre-trained DeiT/LV-ViT. Throughput on RTX 4090, batch 128. Text read is arXiv 2507.16260; the TNNLS version has one more author. No code URL. Not RL.
evidence: "we identify important tokens at each stage and temporarily freeze the unimportant ones, allowing their lagged reusing at a later stage" (Abstract); "We simply employ a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) followed by a Gumbel Softmax [25], [26] to make the binary decision mask" (Sec. IV-B); "We use the pre-trained models to initialize the backbone models and jointly train the entire model" (Implementation Details)

name: MIA-Former
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.9 at 3.9 GFLOPs (head, depth and token skipping; baseline 79.9 at 4.6)
notes: Reinforcement learning (A2C) in a hybrid supervised + RL scheme. A MIA-Controller before each block (CNN/MLP + Gumbel softmax, then A2C actor-critic heads) skips whole blocks, heads and tokens per input; masked tokens pass through a skip connection (operation other, closest to a per-block halt). Training: controller pretraining with blocks fixed, 200-epoch co-training with a FLOPs target, then A2C fine-tuning of controller and blocks from the pre-trained ViT. The reported 79.9 at 3.9 GFLOPs skips heads, blocks and tokens. Token-only skipping gives 79.7 at 3.8 GFLOPs (Table 2). The paper's own unreduced DeiT-S is 79.9 at 4.6 GFLOPs (Table 2), not 79.8. RL stage: 20 epochs plus 50 epochs joint. FLOPs only, no throughput. No code URL.
evidence: "our MIA-Former adopts a low-cost network trained with a hybrid supervised and reinforcement training method to skip unnecessary layers, heads, and tokens in an input adaptive manner" (Abstract); "Note that a skip connection is also added to pass the information of masked heads and tokens to the outputs of the next block" (MIA-Former Framework); "we use an A2Cbased (Mnih et al. 2016) RL learning method to train the MIA-Controller and MIA-Block modules" (Skipping Policy Finetuning with Hybrid RL)

name: TR-PTS
main_result: ViT-B/16: VTAB-1k mean top-1 75.92, 10.35 above full fine-tuning (FLOPs only in Fig. 4)
notes: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning method. Fisher information selects 0.34% of backbone weights to tune (the rest frozen); in parameter-sparse layers the top rho fraction of tokens by [CLS] attention is kept and the rest are averaged into one token (EViT-style fusion). Main purpose is parameter-efficient tuning; token selection is a secondary efficiency component. Inference time measured on A100 at batch 32 (figure only). Not RL.
evidence: "Task-Relevant Token Selection dynamically preserves the most informative tokens and merges redundant ones, reducing computational overhead" (Abstract); "we retain the top ⌊ρN ⌋ tokens based on their attention scores" (Sec. 3.3); "Instead of discarding low-attention tokens, we merge them into a single aggregated token using a weighted averaging process" (Sec. 3.3)

name: RL4EViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.2 at about 3.0 GFLOPs (ViT not fine-tuned; baseline 79.9)
notes: Reinforcement learning (MAPPO, multi-agent PPO in a Markov game). A shared MLP actor makes a keep/prune decision for each token after blocks 3, 6, 9; rewards trade the number of kept tokens against correctness, so the count per layer and image is learned (alpha/beta sets the GFLOPs). The main table trains only the RL parts with the ViT fixed; optional alternating ViT fine-tuning improves accuracy (Fig. 4). Speed on one A6000 (batch size not stated).
evidence: "we model it as a Markov Game and utilize Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO) where each agent makes an individualized pruning decision for a single token" (Abstract); "To be fair to these methods, we disregard fine-tuning in this experiment" (Sec. IV-A); "we allow for optionally fine-tune all the ViT parameters after each update to the token pruning policy" (Sec. III-B)

name: V-Pruner
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.93 at the setting labelled 5 GFLOPS in Table 1 (1847 img/s, 5.5 ms)
notes: Reinforcement learning (PPO). Fisher information (squared gradients of a continuous token mask) gives a per-token prior in the state; the actor outputs per-token keep probabilities and Bernoulli-sampled masks per layer; rewards combine accuracy, Fisher retention, MACs and layer/global budget penalties. Only the policy is trained (1.3 h for DeiT-B); backbone fine-tuning is not described. Table 1 labels DeiT-S as 5 GFLOPS and gives DeiT-B 85.45 and ViT-L 89.27, above the usual baselines; numbers copied as printed. A100; batch size of the latency not stated. Segmentation on VOC/COCO in Table 4.
evidence: "V-Pruner first leverages Fisher information to perform an initial assessment of token importance" (Abstract); "V-Pruner introduces a Reinforcement Learning (RL) Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm, refining token pruning into a global sequential decision process" (Abstract); "we perform Bernoulli sampling to generate a binary decision for each token" (Actor Network and Pruning Execution)

name: PRANCE
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.98 at 2.38 GFLOPs (token merging; baseline 79.90 at 4.70)
notes: Reinforcement learning (PPO) with a 'Result-to-Go' reward. A selector between groups of three blocks picks a per-sample token keep ratio and MHSA/MLP channel widths of a weight-sharing meta-network; tokens are ranked by [CLS] attention, then pruned, merged into the most similar kept token, or pruned-then-merged. Meta-network trained 500 epochs (no initialization from DeiT is mentioned), selector trained 1 epoch on 50k images, then 30-epoch fine-tuning with the selector frozen. In batched inference decisions are averaged over the batch. FLOPs only. Also prunes channels. Text read is arXiv 2407.05010.
evidence: "we design a lightweight selector employing Proximal Policy Optimization for efficient decision-making" (Abstract); "tokens are sorted by their contributions to the task, so that a specific token optimization method can be applied in the second step according to the token keep ratio" (Sec. III-C); "we train the models for 500 epochs using the AdamW optimizer" (Sec. IV, Meta-network)

name: LMFT
main_result: ViT-B/16, Daily-DA M->H: accuracy 74.2 at 217 GFLOPs, 3.9 clips/s (standard tokenization 72.1 at 266)
notes: Video unsupervised domain adaptation. Input tokens whose min-max normalized motion energy (L1 difference of time-averaged patches) is below a threshold tau are dropped before the ViT; tau is learned by reinforcement learning (REINFORCE, logistic-normal policy) and fixed to its expectation at test time, so the count varies per video. VideoMAE ViT-B/16 is trained 20 epochs on source and pseudo-labelled target videos. Main purpose is domain adaptation; token dropping serves both adaptation and efficiency. GPU for clips/s not named (L40 / RTX A6000 used). No code URL.
evidence: "Tokens with overall low motion, falling below a certain threshold (typically corresponding to static or redundant background content), are dropped" (Introduction); "we make the motion threshold learnable using reinforcement learning (RL), since the token selection operation is inherently non-differentiable" (Introduction); "We employ a ViT-B/16 architecture [9], initialized with pretrained VideoMAE weights [27]" (Sec. 5.2)

name: AgentViT
main_result: ViT: Imagenette+ accuracy 58.93 (vanilla 59.95); inference 0.332 GFLOPs and 561 FPS vs 0.675 and 291 (Table 7)
notes: Reinforcement learning (Double DQN). The state is the mean attention per patch from the first ViT layer; patches with Q-value above the mean Q-value are kept and the rest are dropped for the remaining layers. The reward mixes training loss and the number of selected patches. Small ViTs are trained from scratch together with the agent on CIFAR10, FashionMNIST and Imagenette+ (10 ImageNet classes); the stated main goal is shorter training time. Table 7 does not name its dataset. RTX A2000 GPU.
evidence: "For each training batch, the agent observes the attention values generated by the first ViT layer and selects a subset of the original patches to be used during the ViT training process" (Introduction); "selects those with Q-values exceeding the mean Q-value across all patches" (Sec. 3); "we simultaneously trained the underlying SimpleViT and the agent inside AgentSimpleViT" (Sec. 4.2)
